speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: asked	the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) what is the current status of the Hand, Foot and Mouth Disease (HFMD) in childcare centres and preschools; (b) whether more support can be given to parents who have to make alternative arrangements when their children are unable to attend school; and (c) how effective has the Ministry been in tackling challenges faced by parents who have insufficient childcare leave, whose children contracted HFMD more than once in a year, or who are unable to seek childcare support from family members.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: It is a regulatory requirement for preschools to conform to the Ministry of Health's (MOH) guidelines for the prevention and control of infectious diseases.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I would want to repeat that while it is endemic, it is generally a mild disease.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Guidelines include conducting daily health and temperature checks upon arrival, ensuring appropriate hand-washing by staff and children, and having an unwell child rest at the designated sickbay while waiting for the parent or an authorised person to bring the child home.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Centres with two or more suspected or confirmed HFMD cases are required to report the cases to the Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA) and to MOH.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Centres are also required to implement enhanced measures to manage the outbreak of HFMD and are encouraged to conduct self-assessments on health and hygiene.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Centres that experience a high number of sustained cases over a period of time may be required to close.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We understand that this would cause inconvenience to parents.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: However, it is a useful step to break the cycle of transmission of the disease.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Additionally, there have not been local cases in preschools with severe complications due to HFMD.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: To support working parents in caring for their young children, the Government has enhanced child and infant care leave provisions over the years.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Each parent is also entitled to six days of unpaid infant care leave per year during the child's first two years.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: These childcare and infant care leave provisions are in addition to the parents' annual leave provisions.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We also recognise that grandparents and relatives, too, can play an important role in supporting working parents by providing alternative care for their young children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Companies, too, have an important role to play in supporting their employees to manage their work and family responsibilities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: These firms employ 82% of all employees, and this is up from 76% in 2015.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: This is an encouraging development and we want to encourage employers to continue on that trend.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Employers who wish to implement flexible work arrangements can tap on various resources, such as the WorkPro Work-Life Grant.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The tripartite partners also published the Tripartite Advisory on Flexible Work Arrangements to help employers, supervisors and employees implement flexible work arrangements.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We want to see this continue to grow.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We urge parents to tap on these flexible work arrangements and enhanced leave provisions to better manage their work and parenthood responsibilities in caring for their children.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I have one clarification which is, in many of the other services industry, you have services such as home care services whereby physiotherapists go to people's home to provide care.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Will ECDA be exploring the option of having a list of potential nannies or care-givers who can be deployed to homes in the event that the parents have exhausted their leave or are unable to take leave to be at home with their child?

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Because many a times, because of work reason or other reasons, they have already exhausted what available resource they have, and having such external resource may be the only other means for them to care for the children when they contracted HFMD.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We understand the inconvenience affected parents face should a centre close for 10 days, for example.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Right now, as far as we can see, it is an inconvenience but I think parents, by and large, try to manage where they can.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We do urge parents to explore the various possibilities.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We also encourage parents to look at informal arrangements amongst themselves because when a particular childcare centre has some of these closure requirements, the parents could pool efforts among themselves to try to share the responsibilities.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: So, there is a range of different possibilities available.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: I guess if there is a very genuine demand, whether there will be companies or others or private sector sort of solutions that will emerge from that, then, that is something that might occur.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: As of now, as far as we can see, while there are inconveniences, parents try to manage within that range of possibilities that are available to them.
